title: CBDT Exempts TDS on Dividends Between IFSC Aircraft-Leasing Units, Subject to a Form 1(N) Declaration
meta_description: CBDT's Notification 141/2026 exempts TDS on dividends between IFSC aircraft-leasing units, conditional on the payee filing Form 1(N).
case_name: Notification No. 141/2026, Central Board of Direct Taxes
citation: Notification No. 141/2026 dated 4 November 2026, under Schedule VI, Table Sl. No. 11, Income-tax Act, 2025
body: Aircraft leasing out of GIFT City's International Financial Services Centre runs on a layered structure more often than not, with one IFSC unit holding an aircraft or engine and another IFSC unit further up the chain holding equity in the first, sometimes with more than one such layer between the asset and the ultimate investor. Dividends paid between those layered units have, until now, carried a tax-deduction-at-source question that lessors and their tax advisers kept flagging as an unnecessary friction point in an otherwise tax-favourable regime. On 4 November 2026, the Central Board of Direct Taxes issued Notification No. 141/2026 to remove that friction for a defined category of payments.

The notification exempts dividends paid by an IFSC unit primarily engaged in the business of aircraft leasing to another such IFSC unit from the requirement to deduct tax at source, relying on the entry at Table Serial Number 11 of Schedule VI to the Income-tax Act, 2025. Schedule VI is where the new income tax code, which replaced the 1961 Act from this year, gathers a number of specific TDS exemptions that used to sit as scattered notifications, and this entry is the one the CBDT has now operationalised for aircraft-leasing dividends.

That exemption is not unconditional. The paying unit, and in practice the shareholder or payee receiving the dividend, must furnish Form 1(N), a declaration the notification specifies, and the conditions attached to that form have to be satisfied before the exemption can be claimed. Without that declaration on file, the general TDS obligation on dividend payments continues to apply in the ordinary way, so the notification creates a compliance step rather than a blanket, self-executing exemption.

The relief is also narrow in scope by design. It covers dividends paid between IFSC units that are primarily engaged in aircraft leasing, and reporting on the notification is consistent that it does not extend to other categories of IFSC business, to entities outside the IFSC altogether, or to dividend payments that fall outside the specific Schedule VI entry the notification invokes. A unit engaged in ship leasing, for instance, or an aircraft-leasing unit paying dividends to a shareholder that is not itself an IFSC unit, sits outside what this notification covers.

This is not CBDT's first move along this particular track. A notification issued some months earlier, Notification No. 74/2026 dated 3 July 2026, had already applied the same Form 1(N) mechanism to a related but distinct payment stream: lease rent and supplemental lease rent paid by a lessee to an IFSC aircraft-leasing lessor. Read together, the two notifications now cover both ends of a typical aircraft-leasing structure's cash flows, the rent an operating lessee pays up to the leasing unit, and the dividend that leasing unit then pays further up its own ownership chain, with the same declaration-based mechanism governing both.

Sources differ on exactly when the November notification's relief is treated as taking effect, with one account describing it as applying retrospectively from 1 April 2026, which would tie it to the start of the assessment year in which the new Income-tax Act, 2025 itself came into force, rather than to the date the notification was actually issued. Leasing units and their withholding agents should confirm the applicable effective date against the notification text itself before relying on it for dividends already paid earlier in the financial year.

For the aircraft-leasing industry GIFT City has been trying to build, where the economics depend heavily on how cleanly cash can move through a multi-layer IFSC structure without TDS leakage at each layer, a notification like this one is the sort of granular fix that matters more to structuring lawyers and tax teams than it does to anyone outside the sector. Foreign lessors and the Indian promoters setting up IFSC leasing vehicles to attract them should build the Form 1(N) filing into their standard dividend-declaration process now, rather than treating it as an afterthought once a dividend has already been resolved upon.
why_it_matters: IFSC aircraft-leasing structures typically involve dividends moving between layered holding units before reaching the ultimate investor, and uncertainty over TDS at each layer adds real friction to that chain. The notification removes that friction for a defined category of inter-unit dividends, conditional on a Form 1(N) declaration, so foreign lessors and the Indian entities setting up IFSC leasing vehicles should check their dividend-declaration process against this requirement before the next distribution.
card_summary: CBDT's Notification 141/2026, dated 4 November 2026, exempts TDS on dividends paid between IFSC units primarily engaged in aircraft leasing, conditional on the payee filing Form 1(N).
card_tip: Build the Form 1(N) declaration into your IFSC aircraft-leasing structure's dividend process now; the TDS exemption does not apply automatically without it.
verification_notes: The notification number (141/2026), its date (4 November 2026), and its core content (TDS exemption on dividends between IFSC units primarily engaged in aircraft leasing, under Schedule VI Table Sl. No. 11 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, conditional on a Form 1(N) declaration) are corroborated across the Taxmann, Taxscan, The Tax Corp and TeamLease RegTech reports found in this run, which agree on the substance. The related earlier notification (No. 74/2026, dated 3 July 2026, applying Form 1(N) to aircraft lease rent paid to IFSC lessors) is corroborated by a TeamLease RegTech reference in the same search results. Sources disagreed on the effective date, with one describing retrospective application from 1 April 2026 and another giving a different November date; this draft reports the retrospective date as one source's account and flags the discrepancy rather than asserting either as settled, since the notification text itself could not be accessed in this session. No court ruling is involved; this is a regulatory notification reported under the news.md scope's provision for regulator circulars with a specific number and date.
